title: How do I meet God?
theme: Is finding God about searching for Him, or learning to recognize His presence?
opening: There comes a time when the things we once thought important begin to lose their meaning. We find ourselves searching for something more genuine, something that cannot be measured by the world around us. But what exactly are we searching for?
prayer: Lord Jesus,  You know my heart, my struggles, and my longing for what is true.  Help me release the things of this world that draw me away from You. Teach me to recognize Your presence in my life and in the people I encounter.  When I struggle with negativity, renew my hope. When I feel alone, remind me that I belong to You. And when I search for answers, give me the humility to trust what You are revealing.  Holy Spirit, strengthen me from within. Let my heart become a place where Christ may dwell, and may I continue growing in His love.  Amen.
body:
Today, it was the Alleluia before the Gospel that captured my attention:

“I consider all things so much rubbish that I may gain Christ and be found in him.” — Philippians 3:8–9

How deeply these words speak to me.

I find myself increasingly struggling with the ways of this world. I long for genuine truth, genuine fellowship, and the freedom to be myself without the veneer of worldly expectations, past experiences, or the need to be accepted.

As I grow older, I find myself drawn to those who have lived long enough to recognize how little of what we chase truly matters. Life has a way of stripping away our illusions, sometimes through wisdom, sometimes through suffering.

Yet I know that age alone does not bring understanding. We each travel a different road, carrying burdens that others may never see.

And I wonder, through all our searching, what are we hoping will finally make us whole?

I know whom I am searching for. It is Christ.

But knowing this does not mean I have found perfect peace. I still struggle with negativity, unhappiness, and the weight of my own experiences. Sometimes I wonder whether I am truly allowing Christ to fill the emptiness within me.

Perhaps that is where Paul's words offer something deeper.

To be found in Christ does not mean we must first become perfect, free of doubt, or untouched by suffering. It means bringing our whole selves before Him, including the parts we would rather change.

In today's first reading, Paul prays that we may be strengthened through the Holy Spirit and become “rooted and grounded in love.” — Ephesians 3:17

What a beautiful reminder that we are not expected to find our way through life by our own strength.

I still long for fellowship with others who seek the same truth. I still want to become a more joyful, loving person. And I still have much to learn about myself.

But perhaps my search is not about finding something I lack in this world.

Perhaps it is about allowing Christ to reveal what has been waiting within my heart all along: the desire to belong completely to Him.

I do not have to become someone else to be found in Christ. I need only remain open to the One who continues to transform me.

And through the Holy Spirit, I trust that He will continue to guide me, even when I cannot yet see where the journey leads.
